chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: A one-eyed man put out the eye of a sound man. So he said: “His eye is to be put out.” He said: I said: He would remain blind? He said: “The truth has blinded him.”

key_terms.الْحَقُّ: the legal right or just due
key_terms.صَحِيحٍ: sound; one whose eyesight is intact
key_terms.فَقَأَ: put out or destroyed an eye

ai.seo_question: What is the qiṣāṣ ruling if a one-eyed man puts out the eye of a person with sound eyes?
ai.summary: This hadith states a ruling of qiṣāṣ in the case where a one-eyed person destroys the eye of a person with two sound eyes. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام rules that the offender’s remaining eye is to be put out, affirming that legal right is upheld even if it results in his total blindness.
